messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — P0: Elevated 5xx + timeout rate on /v1/generate (region: us-west). Error spike started ~1958502000. Paging oncall @ashley :rotating_light:
ashley: On it. can someone grab initial impact/metrics? which gateway/cluster? cc @mike
mike: us-west gateway b/g -> scheduler pool 'gen-1'. I'm seeing scheduler queue depth climb and HOL blocking from a small subset of very long-context requests. Metrics: queue depth -> 2200 (norm 120), avg batch wait -> 85ms -> 420ms tail.
ashley: timeline?
mike: spike began after ~1958500000, aligns with a rollout from frontend:conversation-history that sends full conversation token sequences to /v1/generate. A few requests are >10k tokens, which blow up batch latency and prevent other batches from dispatching. logs snippet:

```
scheduler: enqueue request id=abcd-1234 tokens=11234 route=gen-1
batcher: hold count=128 wait_ms=420 head_req_id=abcd-1234
worker: dispatch timeout -> client timeout 504
```

jordan: can we temporarily bump capacity or isolate long requests so they don't block the normal small ones?
ashley: yes. mitigation options: 1) enable bypass route for requests < 2k tokens, 2) reduce batch_wait_ms to 10ms, 3) evict/kill >8k token requests for now (return 429 or instruct client to retry), 4) scale up gen-1 pool. Which is fastest?
mike: quickest is bypass rule + batch_wait change. scaling is slower and may not help if HOL persists.
ashley: do bypass + batch_wait. jordan, can you apply bypass policy in routing? sam, can you set batch_wait_ms to 10ms across gen-1?
jordan: applying bypass now. route rule:

```
if tokens_estimate <= 2048 -> route = gen-1-lowlatency
else -> route = gen-1
```

jordan: rule applied (deploy id=deploy-872). deploy-bot: rollout 50% -> 100% in 35s
deploy-bot: rollout complete for route change (deploy-872) at 1958504520
sam: updating batcher config: `batch_wait_ms=10` -> applied on all gen-1 nodes (config-reload triggered)
mike: seeing immediate change: small-request latency drops, but queue depth still high because there are still long requests clobbering workers. We should also throttle or evict the huge ones.
ashley: agree. propose to rate-limit token-heavy requests with a quick filter in gateway to return 429 + guidance.
jordan: added token-threshold reject rule: `if tokens > 8192 -> return 429, body: {"error":"request too large; try summary or shorter context"}`. rule deployed at 1958504660
mike: after bypass + batch_wait + token-reject: queue depth down to 180, 5xx rate dropped from 12.4% -> 2.1% in ~6m. timeouts reduced. customer visible errors still for some in-flight long queries.
ashley: good. who's owning customer callbacks? we need a list of impacted top customers and whether SLA breach.
sam: pulled query logs: 7 customers with >50 timeouts each, including partner-x and analytics-inc. Notifying account reps.
ashley: handoff to @lena for sustained monitoring and postmortem ops. I'm going offline for a quick call. status?
lena: taking over. summary for handoff: mitigation applied (bypass, batch_wait_ms lowered, token-reject), 5xx from 12.4% -> 2.1%, partial customer impact persisted for requests sent before mitigation. I'll keep monitoring for 30m then start RCA.
jordan: note: one long request still stuck on worker node id=node-7 causing elevated worker mem. I've started a graceful drain on node-7 to evict stuck jobs. command used:

```
./nodectl drain --node node-7 --grace 30s
```

deploy-bot: drain initiated (node-7)
mike: after drain, node-7 cleared, worker mem normalized.
lena: current metrics at 1958505820: 5xx=1.9%, avg p95 latency small-requests=78ms, batch_wait average=11ms. Queue depth steady ~30.
ashley: nice work. next steps: 1) rollback conversation-history rollout if that feature is responsible, 2) add server-side token estimation and pre-reject for production, 3) add evict policy to scheduler for head-of-line long-running requests, 4) communicate to customers impacted.
lena: creating incident ticket (INC-2026) and assigning owners. I'll draft customer note with SRE + success.
sam: add follow-up action: we should implement early checksum on client side to avoid sending full history and add a rate-limit/soft-fail option in SDK.
ashley: tag postmortem: RCA owners mike + jordan. I'll join for postmortem. closing oncall to lena at 1958506000. If anything regresses ping here.
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated; severity lowered to P2 at 1958506100. Keep channel open for handoff notes.
lena: monitoring looks stable. I'll run a correlational search for other regions and check if any canary tests were affected. planning to run soft rollback of conversation-history rollout in next 2h.
ashley: thanks team :thumbsup:
jordan: one small note for postmortem: we should add a batching metric export for 'max_tokens_in_batch' so we can alarm earlier.
mike: adding to RFC backlog.
lena: handoff complete. leaving summary and will update ticket with timeline + diffs.
ashley: logging incident as mitigated. final impact estimate: ~6k user requests experienced 5xx/timeouts during 11m window; major customers notified. follow-ups assigned.
incident-bot: incident channel will stay open for 2h for postmortem discussion.
